import Mathlib
open Polynomial MvPolynomial

theorem not_isDedekindRing_mvPolynomial_fin_two {k : Type} [Field k] :
    ¬ IsDedekindRing (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) := by
  intro h
  have hX : (X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) ≠ 0 := X_ne_zero 0
  have hbot : Ideal.span {(X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)} ≠ ⊥ := by
    rwa [Ideal.span_singleton_eq_bot]
  have hprime : (Ideal.span {(X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)}).IsPrime :=
    (Ideal.span_singleton_prime hX).mpr X_prime
  have hmax := Ring.DimensionLEOne.maximalOfPrime hbot hprime
  let I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) := Ideal.span {X 0, X 1}
  have hle : Ideal.span {(X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)} ≤ I := by
    rw [Ideal.span_le]
    intro x hx
    rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
    subst hx
    exact Ideal.subset_span (by simp)
  have hIt : I ≠ ⊤ := by
    intro ht
    have h1 : (1 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) ∈ I := by rw [ht]; trivial
    have hker : I ≤ RingHom.ker (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := k) (fun _ => (0 : k))) := by
      rw [Ideal.span_le]
      intro x hx
      simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
      rcases hx with rfl | rfl <;> simp
    have := hker h1
    simp at this
  have hne : I ≠ Ideal.span {(X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)} := by
    intro heq
    have hX1 : (X 1 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) ∈ I := Ideal.subset_span (by simp)
    rw [heq, Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at hX1
    obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := hX1
    have := congrArg (MvPolynomial.eval (fun i : Fin 2 => if i = 0 then (0 : k) else 1)) hq
    simp at this
  exact hne (hmax.eq_of_le hIt hle).symm
EOF

The proof argues by contradiction using the `Ring.DimensionLEOne` part of `IsDedekindRing`, which requires every nonzero prime to be maximal:

- **The prime `(X 0)`** is nonzero and prime, since `X 0` is prime in the UFD `MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k`.

- So `(X 0)` is a nonzero prime that is not maximal, contradicting the Dedekind hypothesis.
